title: Heat helps cramps
text: Fill a hot water bottle or warm up a heat pad before she asks. Heat on the lower belly or back is one of the most effective cramp relievers.

title: Iron-rich dinner
text: She's losing iron. Cook something with red meat, lentils, spinach or chickpeas. Add a squeeze of lemon or some peppers, because vitamin C helps absorb iron.

title: Check the supplies
text: Quietly check whether pads, tampons, a cup or painkillers are running low and restock them. Ask once which brand she prefers, then remember it.

title: Ask, don't assume
text: Some people want cuddles during their period and others don't want to be touched at all. Ask: "Do you want a hug, or some space?" Both answers are fine.

title: Gentle lower-back massage
text: If she's up for it, a slow, gentle lower-back or belly massage with warm hands can ease cramps. Keep it light and let her guide the pressure.

title: Take over chores
text: Do the dishes, laundry or groceries without being asked and without announcing it. Less to do means more rest for her.

title: Cozy night in
text: Swap the big plans for blankets, a comfort show and takeout. Let her pick the movie.

title: Warm drinks
text: Ginger, chamomile or peppermint tea can soothe cramps and nausea. Bring a mug over without making a big deal of it.

title: Dark chocolate
text: Dark chocolate has magnesium, which can help with cramps and mood. Keep a bar of her favourite in the cupboard for these days.

title: Never blame the period
text: Don't say "is it that time of the month?" when she's upset. Her feelings are real. Hormones can amplify them, but they don't invent them.

title: Let her sleep
text: Fatigue is common. If she wants to sleep in or nap, protect that time: keep it quiet and take care of the morning.

title: Painkillers early
text: Anti-inflammatories like ibuprofen work best taken early, at the first sign of cramps. Have water and her usual painkiller handy if she uses them.

title: Water and less salt
text: Keep a water bottle near her and go easy on very salty food. It helps with bloating and headaches.

title: Offer a gentle walk
text: Light movement can ease cramps for some people. Offer a short, slow walk, with no pressure if she'd rather stay in.

title: No fuss about accidents
text: If there's a stain on the sheets, just say "no problem" and throw them in the wash with cold water. Don't make it awkward.

title: Simple check-in
text: A message like "How are you feeling today? Need anything on my way home?" means a lot.

title: Plan something new
text: Energy and curiosity often rise after the period. It's a great week for a trip, a new restaurant, a class or a hike.

title: Active dates
text: Suggest something active together: climbing, dancing, cycling or a sport. Many people feel strongest in this phase.

title: Fresh and light
text: Try cooking together: fresh salads, fish, fermented foods, and colourful veggies and grains. Cooking together is a date too.

title: Good time for big talks
text: If there's something important to discuss, like plans, money or moving, this phase is often when people feel most open and optimistic.

title: Social plans
text: Many people feel more social now. Good timing for a dinner with friends or a party.

title: Specific compliments
text: Compliment something specific, like her idea, her laugh or how she handled something. Specific beats generic.

title: Date night
text: Around ovulation, confidence and libido often peak. Plan a proper date night: dress up, nice dinner, show her you're into her.

title: Flirt more
text: Leave a flirty message, hold her hand in public, kiss her like you mean it. Many people feel extra attractive in this window.

title: Ovulation twinges
text: Some people feel a short, sharp pain on one side around ovulation. If she mentions it, a heat pad and some sympathy help.

title: Fertile window note
text: This is the most fertile time. The app's estimate is NOT contraception. Use protection you both trust, or talk about family plans openly.

title: Say yes to her ideas
text: If she suggests something spontaneous this week, go for it. Her energy is likely high.

title: Slow it down
text: Energy often dips after ovulation. Swap intense plans for calmer ones: board games, cooking, a quiet walk.

title: Comfort carbs, the good kind
text: Cravings grow in this phase. Sweet potatoes, oats, brown rice or wholegrain pasta help keep energy and mood steady.

title: Magnesium snacks
text: Nuts, seeds, bananas, avocado and dark chocolate are full of magnesium, which may ease PMS symptoms. Leave a snack bowl out.

title: Extra patience
text: Small things may bother her more this week. Don't take it personally. Stay calm, listen, and don't escalate.

title: Run her a bath
text: Run a warm bath with candles and her favourite playlist, then leave her to enjoy it.

title: Protect her sleep
text: Progesterone can make sleep lighter. Keep the evenings calm and the bedroom dark and cool, and don't start late-night arguments.

title: Plan ahead for the period
text: Her period is a week or two away. Check supplies now and keep the days around the predicted start free of big plans.

title: Have her cravings ready
text: Know her PMS cravings (sweet, salty, chocolate, chips?) and have them in the house. Add it to her notes once you find out.

title: Hearty dinner
text: A couple of days before her period, cook a hearty, iron-rich dinner like steak, a beef stew or a lentil curry. It's comforting and refuels her before she loses iron.

title: Listen, don't fix
text: If she vents, don't jump to solutions. Say "That sounds really annoying" and let her talk. Ask if she wants advice before giving any.

title: Give space if asked
text: If she wants alone time, give it gracefully: "Sure, I'm here if you need me." Don't sulk about it.

title: Offer a long hug
text: A long, quiet hug can calm a stressed nervous system. Offer one, and accept it if she says no.

title: Postpone heavy topics
text: Unless it's urgent, save difficult conversations for after her period, when she'll likely feel more like herself.

title: Comfy clothes
text: Bloating is common, so don't comment on her body or what she's eating. If you like, get her a soft hoodie or comfy pants.

title: Reassure her
text: Mood can dip and insecurities get louder. A simple "I love you, I'm on your team" goes a long way.

title: Go easy on caffeine and alcohol
text: Both can make PMS anxiety, sleep and breast tenderness worse. Suggest decaf, herbal tea or a mocktail without lecturing.

title: Headache care
text: Hormonal headaches are common. Dim the lights, bring water and a cold compress, and keep things quiet.

title: Keep the schedule light
text: Avoid booking stressful events (like dinner with your parents) for these days if you can. Keep the weekend flexible.

title: Small surprise
text: Flowers, her favourite snack, or a note saying you appreciate her. Small and unexpected works best now.

title: Don't fight back
text: If she snaps, take a breath before replying. Answer the feeling, not the tone: "You seem stressed. Want to talk?"

title: Careful with touch
text: Breast tenderness is common before a period. Be gentle with hugs and intimate touch, and follow her lead.

title: Ask what helps her
text: Every person is different. Ask her directly: "What helps you most when you're on your period or PMSing?" Save her answers in Her notes.

title: Track it together
text: This works best when she knows about it and helps. Show her the app, let her correct dates, and ask what she'd like you to know.

title: When to see a doctor
text: Very painful periods, cycles that are often shorter than 21 or longer than 35 days, or very heavy bleeding are worth a doctor's visit. Support her in going, and offer to come along.

title: Ask about her day
text: Ask about her day and actually listen. Remember a detail and ask about it tomorrow.

title: Learn her comfort meal
text: Find out her favourite comfort meal and learn to make it well. It helps in any phase.

title: Say thank you
text: Thank her for something small she did. Being appreciated never goes out of season.

title: Respect her time alone
text: Everyone needs some time alone. Encourage her hobbies and friends without feeling left out.

title: Leave a note
text: Hide a small love note in her bag or on the mirror.

title: Car / bag period kit
text: Keep a small kit in your car or bag with pads, painkillers, wipes and a snack. You'll be a hero when it's needed.

title: Not everything is hormones
text: The cycle can affect mood, but don't explain everything with it. If she's upset, there's probably a real reason. Listen first.

title: Plan around the forecast
text: Use the forecast when planning trips or big events. Avoiding the first days of her period can make a holiday much nicer, but ask her first.
